sections.title: Executive investment summary: a cryogenic engineering franchise priced as a compounder

subsections.title: What the company actually does, in plain terms

blocks.text: INOX India Limited designs, engineers, manufactures and installs vacuum-insulated cryogenic equipment - storage tanks, transport tanks and trailers, vaporisers, liquid cylinders, regasification and distribution systems - for gases that must be held near absolute zero. [F] (AR2026 p.65) Products run from 1-litre portable dewars to 1,500,000-litre stationary tanks and transport tanks up to 60,000 litres. [F] (AR2026 p.65) Revenue is earned two ways: standard catalogue products sold against purchase orders and shipped in days to a few months, and long-cycle engineered projects recognised over time under the percentage-of-completion method. [F] (AR2026 p.117) Management put the standard fast-moving share at "almost like 30% to 40%" of revenue and said project orders are now "more than 60%" of the order book, up from about 30% historically. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026), [MC] (CALL May 2026)

blocks.text: The customer base is industrial: 590+ customers served in FY26 across industrial gas majors, LNG operators, space agencies, breweries and research institutions. [F] (AR2026 p.66) Crisil names Air Liquide, Praxair, Linde, ITER and group company INOX Air Products among the clients. [F] (RATING) Three customers, one of them a related party, accounted for 29.09% of FY26 revenue, up from 25.89% in FY25. [F] (AR2026 p.256) The top ten contributed 51% of FY26 revenue. **Listing status and what it means for the evidence base.** The equity listed on BSE and NSE on 21 December 2023 [F] (AR2026 p.133); FY26 is therefore only the second full year of public disclosure. Equity capital has been unchanged at Rs 18 cr since FY22 while reserves grew only with retained profit [F] (NUMBERS), which is consistent with a listing in which the company received no primary proceeds [AI]; the prospectus was not available in this evidence set, so the offer structure and the pre-IPO restated accounts could not be verified. subsections.title: The bear case: ten reasons not to own it

items: **1. The price embeds growth nobody has forecast.** The reverse DCF implies about 77% annual sales growth for five years to justify today's enterprise value, against 14% in the base case and 21.7% actually delivered over five years. [E] (NUMBERS) Bear, base and bull fair values per share are all far below the traded price. [F] (NUMBERS)

**2. Profit is not converting to cash.** Operating cash flow was 0.53x reported profit over three years and 0.45x in FY26 (Rs 117 cr of CFO on Rs 258 cr of PAT). [F] (NUMBERS) Contract assets - unbilled work - rose from Rs 16.3 cr (Apr-2024) to Rs 173.8 cr (Mar-2025) to Rs 385.5 cr (Mar-2026), absorbing Rs 212 cr of cash in FY26 alone. [F] (AR2026 p.257), (AR2026 p.213) The CFO says this 'will remain like this only because the project orders are increasing now'. [MC] (CALL May 2026)

**3. The domestic business did not grow at all in FY26.** India revenue was Rs 604.1 cr against Rs 602.2 cr in FY25 (+0.3%); every rupee of the Rs 281 cr revenue increase came from exports. [F] (AR2026 p.265), [E] The 'India capex cycle' element of the thesis is not visible in the accounts.

**4. Headline margins are flattered by other income.** Management's FY26 EBITDA of Rs 388 cr and margin of 23.8% are struck on total income including other income; our statements data shows EBITDA of Rs 343 cr and a 22% operating margin on revenue from operations. [F] (AR2026 p.66), (NUMBERS) Other income of Rs 45.2 cr included Rs 17.8 cr of forex gains and Rs 10.7 cr of liabilities written back. [F] (AR2026 p.251)

**5. Customer concentration is worsening, not improving.** Top three customers moved from 25.89% to 29.09% of revenue, and one of them is the promoter-group company INOX Air Products. [F] (AR2026 p.256), (AR2026 p.271) Top ten are 51% of revenue. [F] (AR2026 p.67)

**6. Revenue recognition rests on management estimates.** The auditor designated percentage-of-completion revenue on long-term design-build contracts the single key audit matter, citing 'a high degree of judgement' over estimated costs to complete. [F] (AR2026 p.117) With project work now over 60% of the book, the judgement content of reported profit rises. [AI]

**7. Q1 FY27 already missed the growth run-rate.** Revenue from operations grew 9.1% year on year and PAT fell 4.9%; EBITDA was flat at Rs 76 cr with the operating margin down to 20% from 22%. [F] (NUMBERS) Management attributed Rs 32-35 cr of undispatched equipment to freight costs and ship availability, and said disruption continued through July. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**8. Governance economics favour non-executive promoters.** Non-executive promoter directors drew Rs 7.90 cr of commission in FY26 (Siddharth Jain Rs 3.90 cr, Ishita Jain Rs 2.40 cr, Pavan Kumar Jain Rs 1.60 cr) plus Rs 3.97 cr of brand royalty paid to Mr Pavan Kumar Jain personally, against Rs 1.86 cr for the CEO who runs the company. [F] (AR2026 p.272), (AR2026 p.253) There is no managing director on the board. [F] (AR2026 p.71)

**9. A US non-compete has been enforced against the company.** An international arbitral tribunal found INOX India in breach of the Taylor-Wharton America non-compete running ten years from 12 November 2018 and ordered it to pay US$944,657. [F] (AR2026 p.170) The US market - the single largest cryogenic market - is closed to direct manufacturing/distribution presence until November 2028. [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

**10. Single-country manufacturing and a four-plant concentration.** All manufacturing is in Gujarat and the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli; the company itself lists 'dependence on four principal facilities' as a principal risk. [F] (AR2026 p.68), (AR2026 p.81) With 59-62% of revenue exported, freight, tariffs and shipping availability sit directly on the P&L, as Q1 FY27 demonstrated. [F] (AR2026 p.67), [MC] (CALL Aug 2026)

blocks.text: Our variant perception is that the market is valuing INOX India as an Indian industrial-capex and LNG-infrastructure compounder, when the evidence in FY26 describes something different: a niche global exporter of certified cryogenic hardware whose entire incremental revenue last year came from overseas projects, whose domestic business stood still, and whose reported profit is increasingly a function of percentage-of-completion estimates rather than dispatched product. [AI] The engineering franchise is real - the certifications, the ITER and CERN work, the US space orders and the 70-75% domestic tank share are all evidenced [F] (AR2026 p.9), (PPT Aug 2026), (RATING) - but it is a lumpy project business with 0.5x cash conversion, a worsening top-three customer concentration and a governance structure that routes material economics to non-executive promoters. [F] (NUMBERS), (AR2026 p.256), (AR2026 p.272) Against fair values in our DCF of Rs 183-433 per share versus a traded price of Rs 1,979, the gap is not a rounding error in assumptions; the price requires a different company from the one the annual report describes. [F] (NUMBERS)

subsections.title: Where value is captured, and capital intensity

blocks.text: Value is captured at the qualification-plus-design stage, not in fabrication. The evidence is that the company competes for 1,500 m3 space-industry tanks against, on management's account, a single global competitor (Chart Industries) [MC] (CALL Aug 2026), while conceding that Chinese suppliers compete on standard LNG fuel tanks and are held out largely by the PESO approval regime and by service coverage. [MC] (CALL May 2026) Pricing power therefore tracks the code and approval content of each product, not the tonnage. [AI] Management says export realisations run 2-3% above domestic. [MC] (CALL Feb 2026)

On capital intensity, the fixed-asset base is modest - net block Rs 408.7 cr plus Rs 4.2 cr CWIP against Rs 1,587 cr of revenue [F] (AR2026 p.210) - but fixed-asset turnover has fallen from 5.9x (FY20) to 3.71x (FY26) as Savli and Brazil assets were capitalised. [F] (NUMBERS) The real capital is in working capital: inventory Rs 478.2 cr, contract assets Rs 385.5 cr and receivables Rs 312.9 cr against customer advances of Rs 476.4 cr. [F] (AR2026 p.210), (AR2026 p.256) The cash conversion cycle was 238 days in FY26 and working-capital days rose from 44 (FY24) to 61 (FY25) to 83 (FY26). [F] (NUMBERS) This is a working-capital-heavy, fixed-asset-light business - the opposite of how 'asset-light' is usually meant. [AI]

[F] (NUMBERS) **The project-cycle reversion**: the bear case - sales of Rs 2,175 cr on 18% margins, with aerospace revealed as one-off capex, island LNG terminals running at one project every two years, and price competition in standard products.
